children: Bambusa Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharma focused on next‑generation bispecific antibodies for immunology and inflammation, filed for an initial public offering. The company has applied to list its common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “BBTX.” Proceeds will support advancement of lead programs BBT001 and BBT002, pipeline development, and general corporate purposes.

Bambusa Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next‑generation, long‑acting bispecific antibodies designed to address complex immunology and inflammation (I&I) diseases. Its approach combines two validated inflammatory pathways into a single molecule, engineered for extended half‑life and high‑concentration subcutaneous delivery to improve efficacy, durability, and dosing convenience. The company’s lead program, BBT001, targets IL‑4Rα and IL‑31 for atopic dermatitis and other dermatologic conditions, with Phase 1/2 proof‑of‑concept readouts underway. BBT002 targets IL‑4Rα and IL‑5 for respiratory diseases including COPD, CRSwNP, and asthma and has shown dual biomarker effects and favorable safety in healthy volunteers. Two additional programs are in preclinical development: BBT003 (TL1A + IL‑23p19) for inflammatory bowel disease and BBT004 for autoantibody‑driven autoimmune disorders.

Bambusa leverages a clinically validated bispecific antibody architecture originating from BioNTech Zhuhai, incorporates half‑life extension technologies, and prioritizes indications with large, growing markets and unmet needs. Its strategy is to establish clinical proof‑of‑concept in focused indications and expand each asset as a “pipeline‑in‑a‑molecule” across related I&I conditions, while building the late‑stage, regulatory, and commercial capabilities needed for future launches.
: Global I&I market projected to exceed $200 billion by 2030.
: Estimated ~6% CAGR from 2025 to 2030 in I&I.
: Pipeline of long-acting bispecific antibodies with worldwide rights and a clinically validated scaffold; focus on dermatology, respiratory, gastroenterology, and autoimmune diseases.
: Regeneron/Sanofi (Dupixent), Eli Lilly (Ebglyss), Galderma (Nemluvio), GSK (Nucala), AstraZeneca/Amgen (Tezspire), Genentech/Novartis (Xolair), Janssen, AbbVie, BMS, Takeda, among others.
: Shift toward targeted biologics and multi-target bispecifics, half‑life extension for less frequent dosing, expansion of biologics into earlier lines and broader phenotypes.
: Headquarters at 22 Boston Wharf Road, Floor 7, Boston, Massachusetts
: Clinical activity across the United States, Australia, Europe, Georgia, New Zealand, and China
: Research and license agreements with BioNTech (Zhuhai); manufacturing with WuXi Biologics; optioned discovery programs and licensed BBT003/BBT004
: 30 full-time employees as of September 30, 2026; multiple ongoing Phase 1/2 studies and additional preclinical programs targeting first-in-human by 2026–2027
: Loss from operations: $(44.0) million (2025); $(24.1) million (six months ended June 30, 2026)
: Net loss: $(41.1) million (2025); $(22.4) million (six months ended June 30, 2026)

, Chief Executive Officer, President, and Chairperson - Former Vice President at BioNTech leading External Innovations and APAC/China Development; prior equity research experience at major banks; M.D. (Peking University), Ph.D. (UC Irvine), MBA (MIT).

, Co‑Founder and Chief Development Officer - Former Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacometrics Lead at BioNTech; prior roles at Takeda, Vertex, and CytomX; Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering (University of Pittsburgh).
, Chief Financial Officer - Former CFO at Applied Genetic Technologies and Histogenics; Managing Director at Danforth Advisors; investment banking background; MBA (NYU Stern).
, Chief Operating Officer - Former Director of Healthcare Investment Banking at BTIG; prior operational and finance roles in diagnostics; B.A. in Business Communications (UMass).
: BofA Securities, Evercore ISI, UBS Investment Bank, Cantor

: Fund continued development of BBT001 (including Phase 2b AD study) and BBT002 (including a Phase 2b respiratory indication study); advance BBT003 and BBT004; and for capital expenditures, working capital, and general corporate purposes.
